'''Joshua Giddey''' (born 10 October 2002) is an Australian professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Adelaide 36ers]] of the [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] (NBL).

==Early life and career==
Giddey attended St. Kevin's College in Melbourne before emerging as one of Australia's top basketball prospects with the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] Global Academy, a training center at the [[Australian Institute of Sport]] in [[Canberra]].<ref name="uluc2">{{cite web |last1=Uluc |first1=Olgun |title=Josh Giddey emerges out of nowhere to become one of Australia's elite prospects |url=https://www.foxsports.com.au/basketball/josh-giddey-emerges-out-of-nowhere-to-become-one-of-australias-elite-prospects/news-story/321762fc60789f6eca8f8d7da9eb6270 |work=[[Fox Sports (Australian TV network)|Fox Sports]] |access-date=1 April 2020 |date=18 July 2019}}</ref> At the Australian Under-18 Championships in April 2019, he averaged 20 points, 8.3 rebounds and six assists per game, leading VIC Metro to the title.<ref name="pick">{{cite web |title=Josh Giddey: The road so far for Melbourne's next great prospect |url=https://pickandroll.com.au/josh-giddey-the-road-ahead-for-melbournes-next-great-prospect/ |publisher=The Pick and Roll |access-date=1 April 2020 |date=3 October 2019}}</ref> In January 2020, Giddey helped the NBA Global Academy win the Torneo Junior Ciutat de L'Hospitalet in [[Barcelona]], where he earned [[most valuable player]] (MVP) honors.<ref>{{cite web |title=Josh Giddey named MVP as the NBA Global Academy Triumphs at the 2020 Torneo Junio Ciutat de L'Hospitalet |url=https://australia.basketball/blog/2020/01/15/josh-giddey-named-mvp-as-the-nba-global-academy-triumphs-at-the-2020-torneo-junio-ciutat-de-lhospitalet/ |publisher=[[Basketball Australia]] |access-date=1 April 2020 |date=15 January 2020}}</ref> In the following month at [[2020 NBA All-Star Game#All-Star Weekend|NBA All-Star Weekend]] in [[Chicago]], he took part in [[Basketball Without Borders]] and was named an all-star of the camp.<ref name="kidane">{{cite web |last1=Kidane |first1=Benyam |title=Fresh off being named a Basketball Without Borders All-Star and being selected for the Australian Boomers, Josh Giddey continues to make waves |url=https://www.sportingnews.com/au/nba/news/basketball-without-borders-all-star-australian-boomers-josh-giddey-nba-academy/b06khrg3q6xh1cfu5gjrsdql2 |website=[[Sporting News]] |access-date=1 April 2020 |date=18 February 2020}}</ref>

==Professional career==

===Adelaide 36ers (2020–2021)===
On 12 March 2020, Giddey signed with the [[Adelaide 36ers]] of the [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] (NBL) as a part of the league's [[NBL Next Stars Program|Next Stars program]] to develop [[NBA draft]] prospects, and he became the first Australian player to be a part of the program.<ref name="nbl">{{cite web |title=Josh Giddey to Become NBL Next Star with Adelaide 36ers |url=https://nbl.com.au/news/josh-giddey-to-become-nbl-next-star-with-adelaide-36ers |publisher=[[National Basketball League (Australia)|NBL]] |access-date=1 April 2020 |date=12 March 2020}}</ref> Giddey turned down offers from several [[NCAA Division I]] programs, including [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]].<ref name="uluc">{{cite web |last1=Uluc |first1=Olgun |title=Josh Giddey, a 2021 point guard out of the NBA Global Academy picks up offer from Arizona - sources |url=https://www.foxsports.com.au/basketball/josh-giddey-a-2021-point-guard-out-of-the-nba-global-academy-picks-up-offer-from-arizona-sources/news-story/28fd6e08b74baf841eac33b105914267 |work=[[Fox Sports (Australian TV network)|Fox Sports]] |access-date=1 April 2020 |date=26 August 2019}}</ref> On 26 April 2021, he recorded 12 points, 10 rebounds and 10 assists in a 93–77 loss to the [[New Zealand Breakers]],<ref>{{cite web |title=Breakers vs 36ers |url=https://www.fibalivestats.com/u/NBL/1869890/bs.html |work=FIBALiveStats.com |access-date=26 April 2021 |date=26 April 2021}}</ref> becoming the youngest Australian in NBL history to record a [[triple double]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Youngest Australian in NBL history to record a triple double |url=https://twitter.com/NBL/status/1386642755590311940 |work=twitter.com/NBL |access-date=26 April 2021 |date=26 April 2021}}</ref> In the 36ers' next game against the [[Brisbane Bullets]] on 1 May, he became the first ever Australian to record a triple-double in consecutive games, finishing with 15 points, 13 assists and 11 rebounds in a 101–79 win.<ref>{{cite web |title=Night of Sixers celebrations against Bullets |url=https://nbl.com.au/news/night-of-sixers-celebrations-against-bullets |work=NBL.com.au |access-date=1 May 2021 |date=1 May 2021}}</ref> He had a third triple-double on 9 May in a 97–88 overtime win over the [[Sydney Kings]], finishing with 11 points, 12 assists and 10 rebounds.<ref>{{cite web |title=DJ delivers in OT as Giddey racks up another triple-double |url=https://nbl.com.au/news/dj-delivers-in-ot-as-giddey-racks-up-another-triple-double |work=NBL.com.au |access-date=9 May 2021 |date=9 May 2021}}</ref> Giddey was released from the active playing roster on 17 May to prepare for the [[2021 NBA draft]], and finished the season averaging 10.9 points, 7.3 rebounds and a league-leading 7.6 assists per game in 28 games played.<ref>{{cite web |title=Josh Giddey released from Adelaide 36ers active playing roster as Club supports his next step |url=https://www.adelaide36ers.com/news/josh-giddey-released-from-adelaide-36ers-active-playing-roster-as-club-supports-his-next-step |website=Adelaide 36ers |access-date=17 May 2021 |date=17 May 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Uluc |first1=Olgun |title=Josh Giddey released from 36ers' playing roster as he prepares for NBA Draft |url=https://www.espn.com.au/nbl/story/_/id/31458608/josh-giddey-released-adelaide-36ers-playing-roster-prepares-nba-draft |website=ESPN |access-date=17 May 2021 |date=17 May 2021}}</ref> He was selected as the league's [[NBL Rookie of the Year Award|Rookie of the Year]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Bryce Cotton Claims Third Andrew Gaze MVP Trophy |url=https://nbl.com.au/news/bryce-cotton-claims-third-andrew-gaze-mvp-trophy |website=NBL.com.au |access-date=30 June 2021 |date=16 June 2021}}</ref>

===NBA (2021–present)===
On 27 April 2021, Giddey declared for the 2021 NBA draft. He is projected to be a lottery pick.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-04-27|title=Aussie playmaking guard Giddey to enter draft|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/31347794/australian-guard-josh-giddey-projected-lottery-pick-enter-nba-draft|access-date=2021-06-28|website=ESPN.com|language=en}}</ref>

==National team career==
Giddey represented [[Australia national under-17 basketball team|Australia]] at the 2019 [[FIBA]] Under-17 Oceania Championship in [[New Caledonia]]. He averaged 16.4 points, 7.4 rebounds and five assists per game and was named to the All-Star Five after leading his team to a gold medal. In the final against [[New Zealand]], he collected 25 points, eight rebounds, six assists and five steals in an 85–56 win.<ref>{{cite web |title=FIBA U17 Oceania Championship All-Star Five |url=http://www.fiba.basketball/oceania/u17/2019/news/fiba-u17-oceania-championship-all-star-five |publisher=[[FIBA]] |access-date=1 April 2020 |date=25 August 2019}}</ref>

On 23 February 2020, Giddey made his debut for the [[Australia national basketball team]] during [[2021 FIBA Asia Cup qualification]]. He recorded 11 points, six assists and three rebounds in 11 minutes, helping Australia defeat [[Hong Kong basketball team|Hong Kong]], 115–52.<ref>{{cite web |title=Teen Giddey shines on debut in huge Boomers win |url=https://www.smh.com.au/sport/basketball/giddey-debuts-in-huge-boomers-win-20200223-p543jf.html |website=[[The Sydney Morning Herald]] |access-date=1 April 2020 |date=23 February 2020}}</ref> Giddey became the youngest player to play for the senior team since [[Ben Simmons]] in 2013.<ref name="history">{{cite web |title=Giddey set to create history for Boomers |url=https://www.espn.com/nbl/story/_/id/28928239/kings-bogut-delivers-rocket-nbl-admin |website=[[ESPN]] |access-date=1 April 2020 |date=20 February 2020}}</ref>

Giddey was one of the final cuts from the Australian basketball team roster for the [[2020 Summer Olympics|2020 Tokyo Olympics]] and was instead selected as one of three emergency players.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Wenzel |first1=Murray |title=Giddey misses cut as Boomers chase gold |url=https://7news.com.au/sport/basketball/giddey-misses-cut-as-boomers-chase-gold-c-3297938 |website=7 News |access-date=3 July 2021 |date=3 July 2021}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Giddey's father, [[Warrick Giddey|Warrick]], played basketball professionally and was a longtime player for the [[Melbourne United|Melbourne Tigers]] in Australia.<ref name=pick/> His mother, Kim, also played basketball for the Tigers in the [[Women's National Basketball League]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Ward |first1=Roy |title=NBA prospect Giddey learns big lessons in NBL |url=https://www.smh.com.au/sport/basketball/nba-prospect-giddey-learns-big-lessons-in-nbl-20210114-p56u38.html |website=The Sydney Morning Herald |access-date=21 May 2021 |date=16 January 2021}}</ref>
